Data Collection and Processing.PatEx-Bench is grounded in verifiable patent prosecution records
sourced from publicly available USPTO research datasets , which contains examiner-authored OAs.
As official examination decisions issued by qualified USPTO examiners, these OAs carry procedural
legal effect and provide authoritative, professionally validated golden labels rather than synthetic
annotations. For each𝑞𝑖, we retain the first OA and the application in its originally filed version,
including its bibliographic metadata, abstract, specification, and claims, ultimately yielding1Ktasks.
This preserves the initial claims available to the agent instead of the final granted document. To
support prior-art search, we further constructPatent-1MandPaper-52Kfrom publicly accessible
Google Patent and Scholar, respectively. We standardize heterogeneous identifiers and fields into a
unified

assess the quality of the final OA and the evidence grounding of the selected references.(1)We
leverage theevidencescore 𝑠evi𝑖 measures that every entry in the selected reference setE𝑖 is grounded

can be substantially improved by explicitly training search and reasoning capabilities.
Decision accuracy alone does not capture examination quality.Qwen3.6-27B achieves the highest
Decision Accuracy of 87.6%, yet its Score and Select-R remain substantially below those of Claude-
Opus-5-max, at 5.96 vs. 7.34 and 19.5 vs. 32.4, respectively. Decision Accuracy also shows only
moderate rank agreement with the Score, with Kendall's𝜏 of 0.550. These results indicate that
correct final decisions do not necessarily imply equally strong prior-art discovery or overall OA quality.
Additionally, we compute the agreement among the three LLM judges, obtaining Kendall's𝑊= 0.849,
which demonstrates strong consistency in their quality rankings and supports the reliability of our
LLM-based evaluation.
Broader prior-art discovery does not always translate into better reference

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline gains are corroborated by objective recall against official historical USPTO examiner citations and statutory decision labels, which are independent of the LLM judges and synthesis filtering metrics.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Ground-truth examiner-cited reference recall (Search-R, Visit-R, Select-R), statutory decision accuracy, statute F1 against official USPTO office action records, and an ensemble score from three distinct LLM judges.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: SFT on PatEx-SynData trajectories selected via feasibility gating and pairwise tournament ranking over intra-turn NDCG, inter-turn query evolution, LLM-judged evidence grounding, and LLM-judged claim resolution.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported gains align with the empirical findings: PatEx-Agent-4B substantially improves over its base model across the retrieval funnel (+66.8% Search-R, +51.7% Select-R) and demonstrates competitive search capability against much larger models, supported by controlled ablations against random trajectory sampling.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The benchmark evaluation covers 13 LLM baselines and 12 retrieval setups across multiple objective and reference-based metrics (Search-R, Visit-R, Select-R against ground-truth USPTO citations, and statutory decision/ground accuracy) alongside a multi-judge OA quality score. Inter-annotator consistency among the three LLM judges is verified (Kendall's W = 0.849), and comprehensive ablations isolate trajectory filtering quality, search tools, and dense retriever replacements.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline performance and training gains are corroborated by objective recall against official historical USPTO examiner citations and statutory decision labels, which are independent of the LLM judges and synthesis filtering metrics.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Ground-truth examiner-cited reference recall (Search-R, Visit-R, Select-R), statutory decision accuracy, statute F1 against official USPTO office action records, and an ensemble score from three distinct LLM judges.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: SFT trained on PatEx-SynData trajectories filtered via feasibility checks and pairwise tournament ranking across intra-turn NDCG, inter-turn query evolution, LLM-judged evidence grounding, and LLM-judged claim resolution.

primary.limitations: The authors acknowledge that even top frontier models struggle with prior-art recall (Select-R remaining below 33%), and final decision accuracy correlates only moderately with full examination and retrieval quality.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, specifying the execution sandbox environment, toolsets (Boolean, BM25, BGE-M3, and document visit tools), trajectory segmentation by visit anchors, and a 4-dimensional tournament ranking criterion for rejection sampling prior to supervised fine-tuning with environment masking.
primary.quality_rationale: The work provides a well-scoped, rigorously evaluated contribution to agentic search in a demanding domain. Evaluation metrics are objective and grounded in real-world USPTO examiner citations, method descriptions and ablations are thorough, and claim-evidence alignment is strong.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces PatEx-Gym, an agentic framework for patent examination comprising: PatEx-Bench (a 1,000-task benchmark over 1M patents and 52K papers), PASS (an annotation-free trajectory synthesis and tournament-based filtering method leveraging document visits as anchors), and PatEx-Agent (a 4B SFT agent fine-tuned on curated trajectories).

scholarly_quality.rationale: The work provides a well-scoped, rigorously evaluated contribution to agentic search in a demanding domain. Evaluation metrics are objective and grounded in real-world USPTO examiner citations, method descriptions and ablations are thorough, and claim-evidence alignment is strong.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors acknowledge that even top frontier models struggle with prior-art recall (Select-R remaining below 33%), and final decision accuracy correlates only moderately with full examination and retrieval quality.
